m.aarti.dhru: Āratī to you, Sāī Bābā, giver of happiness to all beings! Under the dust of your feet give rest to your servants, give rest to your devotees.
m.aarti.pad1: Having burnt away Kāma, the god of desire, you remain absorbed in your own true Self. To those who long for liberation you show Śrī Raṅga, the Lord, before their very eyes.
m.aarti.pad2: As is the feeling in one's heart, so is the experience you give; O cloud of compassion, such is your wondrous way.
m.aarti.pad3: When one meditates on your name, the suffering of worldly existence is taken away. Unfathomable are your deeds; you show the way to the helpless.
m.aarti.pad4: In the Kali age you are the incarnation, truly the Supreme Brahman with form. Lord Datta Digambara himself has descended as you.
m.aarti.pad5: Every eighth day, on Thursday, devotees make the pilgrimage to see the Lord's feet, which remove the fear of worldly existence.
m.aarti.pad6: Let the service of the dust of your feet be my own treasured wealth; this alone I now ask of you, O God of gods.
m.aarti.pad7: This humble cātaka bird longs for pure water, its only happiness. Give this Mādhava to drink, and keep your promise.
m.shirdi-majhe.abhang1: Shirdi is my Pandharpur, and Sāī Bābā is its Lord, the consort of Ramā (Viṭṭhala).
m.shirdi-majhe.abhang2: Pure devotion is the river Candrabhāgā, and heartfelt feeling is Puṇḍalika, ever awake.
m.shirdi-majhe.abhang3: Come, O come, all you people, and bow down to Bābā.
m.shirdi-majhe.abhang4: Gaṇu says: O Bābā Sāī, run to me and save me, O my mother!
m.naman.abhang1: I will prostrate myself before you and bow at your feet; with my eyes I will behold your form. With love I will embrace you, with joy I will worship you, with devotion I will wave the lamp before you, says Nāmā.
m.naman.shloka2: You alone are my mother and my father; you alone are my kinsman and my friend. You alone are my knowledge and my wealth; you alone are my everything, O God of gods.
m.naman.shloka3: Whatever I do with my body, speech, mind or senses, with my intellect or my self, or out of my own nature, all of it I offer to the Supreme, to Nārāyaṇa.
m.naman.shloka4: I worship Acyuta, Keśava, Rāma, Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, Dāmodara, Vāsudeva, Hari, Śrīdhara, Mādhava, the beloved of the gopīs, the Lord of Jānakī, Rāmacandra.
m.namasmaran.mantra: Hare Rāma Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma Hare Hare; Hare Kṛṣṇa Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Hare Hare: the names of the Lord, chanted with love.
m.namaskarashtak.pad1: O Infinite One, how can I praise you? O Infinite One, how can I bow to you? Even Śeṣa with his countless mouths grows weary singing of you. With all eight limbs I bow to you, Śrī Sāīnātha.
m.namaskarashtak.pad2: Let the mind always remember your feet with devotion; then one lives, by nature, for devotion alone. Thus one crosses the world, carried across, O mother and father. With all eight limbs I bow to you, Śrī Sāīnātha.
m.namaskarashtak.pad3: He who dwells among us to show the play of saints, who to people looks like an ordinary man, yet within is knowledge itself, the giver of liberation: with all eight limbs I bow to you, Śrī Sāīnātha.
m.namaskarashtak.pad4: Fortunate is it that we have gained this human birth; for a person it is truly the means to fulfil life's purpose. Let us hold fast to love for Sāī, so that the ego melts away. With all eight limbs I bow to you, Śrī Sāīnātha.
m.namaskarashtak.pad5: Take this small, ignorant child into your arms; kiss our cheek and make us blessed. With love put a morsel of food into our mouth now. With all eight limbs I bow to you, Śrī Sāīnātha.
m.namaskarashtak.pad6: You whose feet the gods and others worship, to whom Śuka and the sages grant equality with themselves, at whose feet holy places like Prayāga bow in humility: with all eight limbs I bow to you, Śrī Sāīnātha.
m.namaskarashtak.pad7: The cowherd maidens who beheld your feet were ever filled with joy and merged in the Self of pure consciousness; they played the rāsa with Kṛṣṇa, their Lord. With all eight limbs I bow to you, Śrī Sāīnātha.
m.namaskarashtak.pad8: I ask one boon of you, please grant it; with folded hands and deepest humility I pray: carry this Mohinīrāja across worldly existence now. With all eight limbs I bow to you, Śrī Sāīnātha.
m.aisa-yei-ba.dhru: Come thus, O dear one, Sāī Digambara, imperishable incarnation, you who pervade everything, essence of the Vedas, the threefold son of Anasūyā: come, O Bābā, come.
m.aisa-yei-ba.pad1: Every day you bathe and chant at Kāśī, beg alms at Kolhāpur, drink the pure water of the river Tuṅgā, and sleep in the land of Māhur. Come thus, O dear one.
m.aisa-yei-ba.pad2: The alms-bag hangs from your left hand; you bear the trident and the ḍamaru. Ever granting boons and happiness to devotees, you will give the four kinds of liberation. Come thus, O dear one.
m.aisa-yei-ba.pad3: Sandals on your feet, rosary, water-pot and deerskin you carry, O dear one; matted locks coiled like a serpent, a crown shining on your head. Come thus, O dear one.
m.aisa-yei-ba.pad4: Those who are devoted to meditating on you have abundance in their homes for ever; Lakṣmī dwells there day and night; you protect them, warding off all trouble. Come thus, O dear one.
m.aisa-yei-ba.pad5: In this way, O king among Gurus, make your form visible to these eyes; with this body full of the joy of perfect bliss you make us sing the glories of Hari. Come thus, O dear one.
m.mahimna.shloka1: Ever the Self of truth, the root of consciousness and bliss, the cause of the creation, sustenance and dissolution of the world, who out of his devotees' wish shows himself in human form: to that Lord, Sadguru Sāīnātha, I bow.
m.mahimna.shloka2: The sun that destroys the darkness of worldly existence, worthy of praise, beyond mind and speech, reached by the meditation of sages, pervading the world, pure and beyond attributes: to you, the Lord, Sadguru Sāīnātha, I bow.
m.mahimna.shloka3: To uplift the people drowning and suffering in the ocean of worldly existence, who take refuge at his feet and love devotion to him, he took birth in the Kali age: to that Lord, Sadguru Sāīnātha, I bow.
m.mahimna.shloka4: By ever dwelling at the foot of the neem tree he made it pour nectar, though bitter and unpleasant, and made that tree greater than the wish-fulfilling tree: to that Lord, Sadguru Sāīnātha, I bow.
m.mahimna.shloka5: To the people who worship and serve at the foot of that wish-fulfilling tree, seeing it as you, he grants worldly enjoyment and liberation: to that Lord, Sadguru Sāīnātha, I bow.
m.mahimna.shloka6: Whose glorious divine power shines forth through many unheard-of, unfathomable playful līlās, who is free of ego, whose nature is serene: to that Lord, Sadguru Sāīnātha, I bow.
m.mahimna.shloka7: The delightful garden where the good find rest, ever praised by the virtuous who bow to him, who gives joy to people and grants well-being to devotees: to that Lord, Sadguru Sāīnātha, I bow.
m.mahimna.shloka8: The unborn, the first, the one, the Supreme Brahman itself, born of his own will, Rāma himself descended: by your sight, O Lord, I am wholly purified. To the Lord, Sadguru Sāīnātha, I bow.
m.mahimna.shloka9: O Lord Sāī, treasure of grace, giver of every aim and fulfilment to all people: even the Creator cannot describe the matchless power of the dust of your feet. With true devotion and folded hands I have come to you for refuge, O Lord. Apart from the lotus feet of the glorious supreme Lord Sāī I have no other refuge.
m.mahimna.shloka10: Day and night, with joy, I meditate on the Lord, the best of the Rāghavas who has taken the form of Sāī, the wish-fulfilling tree of his devotees, to purify a mind struck by māyā.
m.mahimna.shloka11: O Sāīnātha, may your umbrella of grace, bright as the autumn moon, by its cool shade remove the burning distress of those who have taken refuge at your lotus feet.
m.mahimna.shloka12: O Sāīnātha, deity of my worship, praised by me, Upāsanī, with these hymns: may my mind delight in your two feet as a bee, eager for honey, delights in the lotus.
m.mahimna.shloka13: By the sight of your lotus feet the sins gathered over many births are destroyed. Forgive all my heaps of faults; be gracious, O Lord Sāī, O Guru, treasure of compassion.
m.mahimna.shloka14: Those whose minds are purified by the nectar of Śrī Sāīnātha's feet, who are ever devoted to serving those feet with love, are freed from the flood of sins born of worldly existence and attain the supreme abode of liberation.
m.mahimna.shloka15: The person who always recites this hymn with devotion, with the mind fixed on him, surely becomes worthy of the grace of Sadguru Sāīnātha.
m.dashak.pad1: Let my beloved mother be displeased with me, let even my father be displeased; let my beloved wife be displeased, and even my dear son and daughter. Let my sister and brother, my father-in-law and mother-in-law be displeased; but may Datta-guru, Sāī my mother, never be displeased with me.
m.dashak.pad2: Let my daughter-in-law not ask after me, nor my brother's wife; let my dear relatives, my own kin and my community not ask after me. Let no well-wisher, friend, my own people or close kinsmen ask after me; but may the Guru, Sāī my mother, never be displeased with me.
m.dashak.pad3: Let women and children not ask after me, nor the young, nor even the old; let neither elders nor juniors, neither the great nor the small, ask after me. Let no one, good or bad, ask after me, not even good people and saints; but may the Guru, Sāī my mother, never be displeased with me.
m.dashak.pad4: Let the clever and the knowers of truth be displeased, the learned, the wise and the men of knowledge; let even learned women and skilled women scholars be displeased. Let kings and renunciants be displeased, worshippers and even ascetics; but may Datta-guru, Sāī my mother, never be displeased with me.
m.dashak.pad5: Let poets, seers and sages, the sinless siddhas and the yogis be displeased; let even the household deity be displeased, and the family goddess and the village goddess. Let wicked fiends and foul she-demons be displeased too; but may Datta-guru, Sāī my mother, never be displeased with me.
m.dashak.pad6: Let beasts, birds, insects and all living creatures be displeased; let trees, stones, mountains, rivers and oceans be displeased. Let space, air, fire, water and earth, the five elements, be displeased; but may Datta-guru, Sāī my mother, never be displeased with me.
m.dashak.pad7: Let the pure kinnaras and the stainless yakṣiṇīs be displeased; let the moon, the sun and the planets, and the stars in the sky be displeased. Let even Indra, king of the gods, be displeased, and Yama, the merciless lord of death; but may Datta-guru, Sāī my mother, never be displeased with me.
m.dashak.pad8: Let my mind and my speech be displeased, and that fickle intellect too; let my body and all the directions be displeased, and relentless Time as well. Let the whole world be displeased with me, even the entire universe; but may Datta-guru, Sāī my mother, never be displeased with me.
m.dashak.pad9: Let people laugh at me and call me a fool, but let envy never sting me; may my love for your feet keep growing, and may I not be caught in the mire of birth and death. May the fortress of my steadfastness never fall, may unholy feelings fall away; may this mind turn from worldly life, and firm dispassion be set in my heart.
m.dashak.pad10: May I hate no one and long for nothing; may Sāī always dwell in my heart, in my mind and in my meditation. May love for your feet well up in me, may I see Bābā in all that is seen; and may Datta-guru, Sāī my mother, not be displeased at this prayer.
m.pushpanjali.mantra1: Through sacrifice the gods worshipped the Lord of sacrifice; these were the first acts of dharma. The great ones attained the heavenly world where the Sādhyas, the ancient gods, dwell.
m.pushpanjali.mantra2: To the king of kings, who conquers by his might, we bow; to Vaiśravaṇa we offer worship. May he, the lord of desires, Vaiśravaṇa, grant me, who long for fulfilment, all I desire. To Kubera Vaiśravaṇa, the great king, salutations.
m.pushpanjali.mantra3: May there be well-being. May our king have universal rule, enjoyment, self-rule, distinguished rule, the highest station, kingship, great kingship and lordship; may he be ruler over all the earth, of long life, to the farthest end of time, sole sovereign of the earth bounded by the oceans.
m.pushpanjali.mantra4: Of this the verse is sung: the Maruts dwelt as attendants in the house of Marutta, son of Avikṣit, whose every desire was fulfilled, and the Viśvedevas were the members of his assembly.
m.pushpanjali.jay1: Glory to Śrī Nārāyaṇa Vāsudeva, Saccidānanda, Sadguru Sāīnātha Mahārāja!
m.prarthana.shloka: Whatever wrong I have done with hands or feet, by speech or body or action, through ears or eyes, or in the mind, in doing what was enjoined or what was not, forgive all of it. Glory, glory to you, ocean of compassion, Lord Sāīnātha!
m.prarthana.jay2: Glory to Śrī Saccidānanda Sadguru Sāīnātha Mahārāja!
m.prarthana.jay3: Glory to the Lord of countless millions of universes, King of kings, King of yogis, the Supreme Brahman, Śrī Saccidānanda Sadguru Sāīnātha Mahārāja!
